sections.h2: What the Shelby County probate office does in a home sale
sections.html:
In Shelby County the judge of probate is the officer who accepts your signed deed into the public record. The office also collects Alabama's recordation tax at the counter. Under section 40-22-1, no deed or similar instrument is taken for record until that privilege tax has been paid, so the money and the document arrive together.

Two stops follow every closing. The first is probate, where the deed is recorded. The second is the county revenue office, where the property is assessed and you show the deed. Phone the probate office for its fee sheet before you promise a buyer a closing day.

sections.h2: How the deed tax is calculated
sections.html:
Alabama charges 50 cents on each $500 of value that changes hands, and any leftover fraction of $500 counts as a full unit. The measure is the real price paid. Under section 40-22-1(c), a mortgage or vendor's lien that already paid its own mortgage tax comes off the base, so only the value above that debt is taxed.

Every deed needs proof of the true price, written on a Department of Revenue form. Whoever signs it vouches in good faith that the number is right. When no proof is offered, the judge of probate falls back on the latest assessed value and adds a penalty. A person who knowingly holds back proof after being asked owes $100 or 25 percent of the tax actually due, whichever is larger.

Deed tax rules under section 40-22-1
TopicRule
Rate$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction
Tax baseActual price, less mortgage or lien that paid mortgage tax
Split of the taxTwo thirds to the state, one third to the county
Penalty for withheld proof$100 or 25 percent of tax due, whichever is greater
No tax requiredNominal-consideration title-perfecting deeds, corrected deeds, mortgage transfers that already paid

sections.h2: Exempt deeds and land in two counties
sections.html:
Some papers go on record with no tax. These are deeds written for nominal consideration to perfect title, re-recorded corrected instruments, and transfers of mortgages that already paid their tax. On an exempt deed the judge of probate applies a "No Tax Collected" stamp.

Land lying in more than one county gets different handling. The probate judge sends the instrument to the Department of Revenue, and the Department assigns a value to each county's share. To avoid waiting, the filer may leave an estimated sum and record at once. If the estimate was too high, the extra comes back after the value is set.

Several Shelby County communities straddle a county line: Vestavia Hills, Hoover, Helena, Leeds and Calera. Your title company will check whether the parcel sits wholly in one county.

Shelby County is in central Alabama, with Columbiana as its seat. Residents numbered 66,298 in 1980 and 223,024 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 238,552. The 2020 count showed 84,241 households and 89,060 housing units, with 78.1 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners. Interstate 65 and U.S. 31 tie the county to Jefferson County, and the suburban boom in Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea followed those roads.

Arrive at the counter with a signed deed, an accurate legal description and a finished price form. A deed that needs fixing costs you time in line.
Parts of the county run along the Cahaba River, the Coosa River valley and Lay Lake. Owners of lakefront or riverside lots should check flood maps with their insurer and the county before listing.

sections.h2: Common snags at the probate office
sections.html:
Paper causes most delays here. Typical trouble spots:

  • A wrong legal description or a misspelled owner name, which may call for a corrected deed.
  • Missing proof of the purchase price, which brings the value penalty.
  • An unpaid property tax bill, because Alabama taxes become delinquent after December 31.
  • An owner who has died, which can mean the estate needs a court order before the house can be conveyed.

Alabama counties need not mail tax notices, so an owner who never got a bill still owes the tax. Buyers should ask the county about payment status before the deed goes on record.

Count backward from the recording step. Get the fee sheet from the probate office, then agree with your closing attorney or title company on who carries the deed to the counter and who supplies the price form. Every owner's name should match the prior deed letter for letter, and the legal description should be checked against it. If the parcel may touch a second county, say so early so the Department of Revenue step does not catch anyone off guard.

Tax timing matters too. With delinquency starting after December 31, a closing near year end needs a firm answer on what has been paid. Ask the county for the status and list any balance on the closing statement so it comes out of the seller's proceeds.

An estate may need a court order before the house can be conveyed. Ask the probate office what paperwork the court expects, and collect the death certificate and any will. See an attorney before you list. Every buyer, cash or financed, wants clear authority to sign, and a missing order is a common reason a closing slips.

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
A short packet saves a second trip.

  • The signed and notarized deed with a correct legal description.
  • The Department of Revenue form proving the actual price paid.
  • Payment for the recordation tax and the recording fee.
  • A copy of the deed for the county revenue office, where the property is assessed next.
  • Any court order, if an estate or a two-county parcel is involved.

If anything on the list is missing, the clerk cannot accept the deed for record, and the closing may have to wait for another visit.

sections.h2: From signed deed to new owner
sections.html:
Begin with a signed deed carrying the right names and legal description, notarized as your closing attorney directs. Staple on the proof of the actual price. Take both to the probate office with money for the tax and the recording fee, which a phone call will confirm. The clerk records the deed. Next, bring a copy to the county revenue office so the property is assessed in the new owner's name.

Cash buyers pay the same tax and recording costs as everyone else. What a cash sale changes is the repair list and the wait on a lender, and the recording steps stay the same.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Shelby County, Alabama?
faqs.a: The judge of probate takes the deed for record. After that, the new owner has the property assessed at the county revenue office.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax rate in Alabama?
faqs.a: It is $0.50 per $500 of value, with any fraction of $500 counted as a full unit, and a mortgage or lien that already paid its tax is subtracted. The state gets two thirds and the county one third.

faqs.q: Do I have to show the sale price when I record a Shelby County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Proof of the real price must come with the deed on a Department of Revenue form. Knowingly withholding it after a request costs $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is larger.

faqs.q: Is any deed recorded without tax?
faqs.a: A few are. Title-perfecting deeds for nominal consideration, corrected deeds and mortgage transfers that already paid are exceptions, and the judge of probate marks them "No Tax Collected."

faqs.q: What are the recording fees in Shelby County?
faqs.a: Phone the probate office for the current schedule before closing.
